key_insight: Mixing nanoscale Laponite with microscale Bentonite reduces drying damage, with most intermediate compositions on glass outperforming a simple average of the pure clays.
engineering_relevance: Clay composition offers a practical lever for reducing cracking and peeling in coatings, barrier layers and ceramic processing.
method: Compare drying damage across clay compositions on hydrophobic polypropylene and hydrophilic glass.
Measure two-step yielding in gelled suspensions and derive cohesive energies.
Use an energy-balance-derived cohesion–adhesion index to interpret cracking versus peeling.
evidence_signal: Replicate experiments support essentially intact Laponite films, extensive Bentonite fracture and reduced damage in mixtures; inferred cohesive energies vary by orders of magnitude between yield steps.
watch_item: Rheology–cracking correlations must specify the yield step used, and composition-dependent critical crack-free thickness remains unresolved.
paper_title: Resisting Drying Stress in Laponite Bentonite Clay Composites, Two Step Yielding and Crack Peel Selection
